prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1330; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was stationary when struck by a third-party vehicle while backing out of a space. Both drivers exchanged information at the scene. Liability appears clear on the third-party driver's side pending the statement review.

Entry 2: Claimant's vehicle inspected via photos. Rear bumper damage and minor cracking to the tail light assembly noted. Estimate requested from preferred repair facility. Claimant reports neck strain following the impact and has since retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 3: Received letter of representation from claimant's attorney. Attorney requests a copy of the police report and the scene photographs. Documents sent. Medical authorization forms forwarded to the attorney for the claimant's signature. Diagnosis on file indicates cervical strain with a recommendation for physical therapy.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of the medical records. Records from the treating clinic are still pending. Attorney indicated the client has completed six physical therapy sessions and is continuing treatment. Reminded counsel that the bodily injury evaluation cannot be finalized until the records are received and reviewed.

Entry 5: Repair estimate reviewed and approved for the insured vehicle. Subrogation file opened against the third-party carrier. Bodily injury reserve reviewed and kept at current level pending receipt of the treatment records. Follow-up scheduled to check on records status with the claimant's attorney's office.
